takeaway: Painful, swollen limb in a plaster, even with a distal pulse: suspect compartment syndrome. Remove the plaster first and reassess; fasciotomy is the definitive treatment.

lines.text: A young man has a lower limb plaster after a complex tibial plateau fracture.
Now his limb is painful and swollen, yet a distal pulse can still be felt.
Do not be reassured by the pulse. This is compartment syndrome, caused by external compression from the plaster.
The immediate step is to remove the plaster, and then reassess the patient.
The definitive treatment is a fasciotomy.
Suspect compartment syndrome when pain is out of proportion to the injury, or on passive stretch of the compartment. Paralysis and paraesthesia are late signs.
